title: Interpret Load Direction vs Unload Direction Between Cells for AGV Tote Access
summary: Use the cell-to-cell load/unload direction settings to determine which AGVs are permitted to travel between two cells: unload direction allows AGVs without a tote; loaded direction allows AGVs with a tote. If both are enabled, both tote states can travel between the cells. If the observed behavior contradicts the configured direction permissions, treat it as a design/map issue and escalate rather than attempting an operator-level fix.
when_to_use: When you need to interpret the tote-dependent travel permissions between two cells based on the load/unload direction settings visible in the cell-to-cell configuration context.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to perform a configuration change or to attempt to correct a load/unload direction problem directly on the live system.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Interpret the configured load/unload direction permissions between two cells (tote vs no-tote travel) and determine whether the issue is consistent with the configuration.
Escalation owner (per site/support process): Handle cases where the system behavior does not match the configured direction permissions (treated as a design problem).
access_or_tools_needed: OptiSweep map/cell configuration view that shows load direction and unload direction between cells

visual_references.description: Training frame showing cell selection (node code/cell code) and the explanation of unload direction vs loaded direction between two cells, including the tote/no-tote travel permission rules and note that most areas have both turned on.

steps.title: Locate the load/unload direction settings for the connection between two cells
steps.purpose: Identify the configured direction permissions that determine whether AGVs with a tote, without a tote, or both can travel between the two cells.
steps.instruction: In the OptiSweep map/cell configuration context where the cell-to-cell connection is visible, locate the fields for unload direction and loaded direction for that specific connection between the two cells.
steps.expected_result: You can see whether unload direction and/or loaded direction are activated for the connection between the two selected cells.
steps.healthy_condition: Both unload direction and loaded direction fields are visible for the connection, and their activated/not-activated state can be determined.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine the activated state of unload direction and loaded direction for the connection between the two cells.

actions.label: Find unload/loaded direction fields for the cell-to-cell connection
actions.exact_action: Locate the settings for the connection between the two cells in the map/cell configuration context where load direction and unload direction between cells is visible.

steps.title: Interpret unload direction-only activation (no tote travel allowed)
steps.purpose: Determine the tote-dependent travel permission when only unload direction is enabled between the two cells.
steps.instruction: If only “unload direction” is activated between the two cells (and loaded direction is not), conclude that only AGVs without a tote can travel there.
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion is: only AGVs without a tote are allowed to travel between the two cells.
steps.healthy_condition: The configuration shows unload direction enabled while loaded direction is not enabled for that connection.
steps.failure_condition: The configuration does not clearly show unload direction-only activation, or you cannot confirm that loaded direction is not enabled.

actions.label: Check unload direction-only state
actions.exact_action: Check whether only “unload direction” is activated between the two cells.

steps.title: Interpret loaded direction-only activation (tote travel allowed)
steps.purpose: Determine the tote-dependent travel permission when only loaded direction is enabled between the two cells.
steps.instruction: If only “loaded direction” is activated between the two cells (and unload direction is not), conclude that only AGVs with a tote can travel between those cells (AGVs without a tote cannot).
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion is: only AGVs with a tote are allowed to travel between the two cells.
steps.healthy_condition: The configuration shows loaded direction enabled while unload direction is not enabled for that connection.
steps.failure_condition: The configuration does not clearly show loaded direction-only activation, or you cannot confirm that unload direction is not enabled.

actions.label: Check loaded direction-only state
actions.exact_action: Check whether only “loaded direction” is activated between the two cells.

steps.title: Interpret both load and unload direction activation (both tote states allowed)
steps.purpose: Determine the tote-dependent travel permission when both direction permissions are enabled between the two cells.
steps.instruction: If both unload direction and loaded direction are turned on between the two cells, conclude that both AGVs with a tote and without a tote can access travel between those cells.
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion is: both tote and no-tote AGVs are allowed to travel between the two cells.
steps.healthy_condition: The configuration shows both unload direction and loaded direction enabled for that connection.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm that both direction permissions are enabled for the connection.

actions.label: Check both directions enabled
actions.exact_action: Check whether both load and unload direction are turned on between the two cells.

steps.title: Escalate if observed behavior contradicts configured direction permissions
steps.purpose: Avoid incorrect operator-level remediation when the source frames direction behavior as a design problem.
steps.instruction: If the system behavior you observe does not match the tote-dependent travel permissions implied by the configured load/unload direction settings between the two cells, stop and escalate. Treat it as a design/map issue rather than something support should fix at the operator level.
steps.expected_result: You stop attempting fixes and escalate the mismatch as a design problem.
steps.healthy_condition: The configured direction permissions are clear, and the observed behavior is inconsistent with those permissions.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to resolve the mismatch via operator-level actions instead of escalating.

actions.label: Stop and escalate direction mismatch
actions.exact_action: If the source’s described direction behavior does not match what the system appears to allow, stop and escalate.

stop_or_escalate_if: Observed behavior contradicts the tote/no-tote travel permissions implied by the configured unload/loaded direction activation between the two cells.

success_criteria: You can state, based on the activated unload direction and/or loaded direction between two cells, whether AGVs with a tote, without a tote, or both are allowed to travel between those cells.
healthy_conditions: Unload direction-only: only AGVs without a tote are permitted between the two cells.
Loaded direction-only: only AGVs with a tote are permitted between the two cells.
Both enabled: both tote and no-tote AGVs are permitted between the two cells.
failure_conditions: You cannot determine the activated state of unload direction and loaded direction for the connection between the two cells.
Observed behavior contradicts the configured direction permissions; you proceed with operator-level fixes instead of escalating.
escalation_guidance: Escalate when observed behavior does not match the configured load/unload direction permissions. The source frames load/unload direction issues as a design problem, not something support should deal with at the operator level.
